title: Restricted typicality in non-equilibrium quantum many-body systems
authors: Konrad Pawlik, Piotr Sierant, Jakub Zakrzewski
abstract: Characterizing the time evolution of generic quantum many-body systems is a fundamental challenge, as representing the exact state requires exponentially scaling computational resources. While hydrodynamics and statistical mechanics successfully simplify this task by predicting the expectation values of local observables, these macroscopic frameworks provide no information about nonlinear characteristics of the quantum state. In this work, we demonstrate that for systems exhibiting a timescale separation, with dynamics governed by the transport of conserved charges, this lost information can be systematically recovered. By constraining the maximum-entropy Scrooge ensemble solely by the system's slow modes, we accurately reconstruct complex, nonlinear quantum properties of the global time-evolved state, including the half-chain entanglement entropy and the participation entropy in the computational basis. Our results generalize the paradigm of canonical typicality, revealing that a hydrodynamically bottlenecked system behaves as a typical pure state within a dynamically restricted submanifold of the Hilbert space - a phenomenon we term global restricted typicality.
summary: This paper addresses the challenge of tracking complex quantum many-body dynamics by introducing the 'Scrooge ensemble.' By constraining this maximum-entropy ensemble only with the expectation values of slow, conserved modes, the authors demonstrate a principle called 'global restricted typicality.' This allows for the accurate reconstruction of nonlinear quantum properties, like entanglement entropy, even when standard hydrodynamic methods are insufficient.
main_problem: Characterizing the time evolution of generic quantum many-body systems is computationally intractable due to the exponential scaling of state representation.
main_result: The authors introduce 'global restricted typicality,' showing that complex, nonlinear quantum properties can be accurately reconstructed by constraining the maximum-entropy Scrooge ensemble using only the system's slow, conserved modes.
method: The core method involves constructing the Scrooge ensemble, which maximizes information entropy subject to fixing the first statistical moments (expectation values) of the slow modes, thereby bypassing standard coarse-graining assumptions.
model_or_system: The work applies to generic quantum many-body systems, particularly those exhibiting a timescale separation where dynamics are governed by the transport of conserved charges, such as those studied in quantum hydrodynamics.
key_observables: Entanglement entropy (half-chain) and participation entropy in the computational basis.
important_parameters: Timescale separation, slow modes (conserved charges), and the constraints derived from the system's slow dynamics.
main_assumptions: The approach assumes a timescale separation and that the dynamics are governed by the transport of conserved charges, allowing the slow modes to constrain the global state.
figures_summary: Figure 1 conceptually illustrates global restricted typicality, showing the time-evolved state lying on a dynamically restricted manifold, and outlines the operational pipeline from microstate to the Scrooge ensemble.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theoretical framework by defining the Scrooge ensemble, applying it to systems with slow dynamics, and demonstrating its ability to recover nonlinear quantum properties by constraining the ensemble solely with slow mode expectation values.
why_interesting: It provides a powerful, non-standard statistical tool (the Scrooge ensemble) to extract global, non-linear information about non-equilibrium quantum states, bridging the gap between local observables (hydrodynamics) and full quantum state characterization.
